Dairy industry view

MPO: Dairy herd vaccination and FMD case burden.

Submitted by the Milk Producers’ Organisation (MPO). Covers dairy cattle only.

Dairy cows vaccinated by province: dose 1 and dose 2.

Active dairy FMD farms by province.

Farm status over time.

Weekly count of dairy farms with confirmed and active FMD nationally.

Post-vaccination reinfections.

Farms that reported FMD reinfection after receiving vaccine. Clinical signs in reinfected herds have been significantly less severe than pre-vaccination outbreaks — consistent with vaccine protection moderating disease severity.

Active dairy FMD farms and vaccination progress by province.

Industry distribution view

RMIS: Industry vaccine distribution.

Tracked by the Red Meat Industry Service (RMIS). Covers the private industry channel — doses allocated to and distributed by industry across all sectors (feedlot, commercial farms, stud). Complements the state programme doses tracked in the provincial data above. Cumulative from rollout start.

Doses distributed by province and manufacturer.

Doses by sector.

Top districts by doses distributed.

Cumulative feedlot orders over time.

Manufacturer split.

Data notes.

The RMIS industry channel covers vaccine distributed directly to farmers and feedlots through private veterinary practices, separate from state-programme doses administered by provincial veterinary services. Source: RMIS weekly Excel exports; the as-at date is shown on the cards above. Biogenesis = Biogenesis Bagó (Argentina). DolVet = DolVet Biotech Trivalent (Turkey).

Pork industry view

SAPPO: Pig sector vaccine dispatches.

Submitted by the South African Pork Producers' Organisation (SAPPO). Covers Aftodoll (Dollvet) vaccine dispatched by SAPPO representatives to pig producers across South Africa. Some bottles were also used for cattle on the same farms to reduce cross-species FMD risk — the cattle/pig split is not available at dispatch level. Source: email from Dr Thandi Chiappero, SAPPO Head: Consumer Assurance, 3 June 2026.

Ministerial and ICC update

The Foot and Mouth Disease Industry Coordination Council is a task team established by the Minister of Agriculture, so we report Ministerial and ICC updates as a single source.

    Data validation

    Ministerial briefing vs JOC provincial returns.

    Comparing DAFF ministerial figures (4 June 2026) against AgriSA JOC provincial returns (latest available). A positive difference means JOC reports more vaccinations than the ministerial figure — expected given the later date. A negative difference flags a data quality issue for investigation.

    Animals vaccinated: ministerial vs JOC per province.

    Province Ministerial

    Latest    		 Difference Status

    Ministerial figures cover all cloven-hoofed animals. JOC returns may be cattle-only in some provinces — explaining part of the gap.

    Vaccine ordering

    How to order FMD vaccine as a private individual.

    We set out the three approved routes to order foot and mouth disease vaccine for your own herd below. All three report vaccination detail back to the National Department of Agriculture, so the route you choose does not affect your compliance standing. Choose the route that matches how your farm and your veterinary relationship are already set up.

    1

    Government.

    Through your state veterinarian.

    Choose this if You already work with your state veterinarian.
    Who runs it: Department of Agriculture.
    Vaccine: ARC, Biogenesis Bago, Dollvet.
    1

    Phone your state veterinarian and ask to order vaccine.

    2

    Your state veterinarian sends your order to the Department of Agriculture.

    3

    After vaccinating, send your farmer, animal and vaccination detail to the Department.

    Go to the FMD reporting system

    Support line 0860 246 640
    FMDcommandcent@nda.gov.za

    2

    Industry.

    Through the RMIS portal.

    Choose this if You already work with a private veterinarian.
    Who runs it: RMIS, RPO, SAFA, SBF, MPO, SAPPO and AFASA.
    Vaccine: Biogenesis Bago.
    1

    Ask your private veterinarian to order on your behalf. Stud and milk farmers may order through IDTrax instead.

    2

    Your veterinarian places the order on the RMIS vet ordering portal.

    3

    After vaccinating, load the detail onto any record keeping system linked to the traceability platform.

    Go to the RMIS ordering portal

    RMIS operational centre
    067 391 4530

    3

    Private.

    Order it yourself, online.

    Choose this if You want to order directly yourself.
    Who runs it: Buffalo Analytics, with the vaccine importer Dunevax.
    Vaccine: Dollvet, Aftodoll-oil.
    1

    Register on Buffalo Analytics and place your order yourself.

    2

    Your private veterinarian reviews and signs the prescription.

    3

    After vaccinating, load the animal and vaccination detail onto Buffalo Analytics.

    Go to Buffalo Analytics

    Platform
    www.buffalo.vet

    The order and delivery journey, in six steps.

    Whichever route you choose, the journey is the same.

    1

    Order.

    Place your order through your veterinarian or your chosen platform.

    2

    Confirm.

    Your order is checked against stock and an invoice is sent to you.

    3

    Pay.

    You pay and your order is confirmed.

    4

    Deliver.

    The vaccine is couriered to your veterinary practice.

    5

    Vaccinate.

    Your animals are vaccinated and the batch detail is recorded.

    6

    Report.

    The vaccination detail is loaded onto the system for your route.
